profile.name: Tanbir Hasan
profile.tagline: Designing with precision. Simulating with confidence.
profile.bio: I am a Mechanical Design and Simulation Engineer specializing in 3D CAD modeling with SOLIDWORKS and computational analysis (CFD & FEA) with ANSYS. I combine rigorous engineering fundamentals with advanced simulation to design, validate, and optimize mechanical systems.
profile.heroSubtitle: A portfolio of precision-engineered 3D designs and validated simulations across CAD, CFD, and FEA.

aboutSections.heading: What I Do
aboutSections.text: I design mechanical components and assemblies in SOLIDWORKS, then validate them through finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics in ANSYS. My workflow bridges concept sketches to production-ready models backed by simulation data.

aboutSections.heading: My Approach
aboutSections.text: Every design starts with understanding the physics. I believe simulation should inform design decisions early — not just verify them at the end. This iterative approach reduces prototyping cycles and produces more robust, optimized solutions.

designs.title: Spur Gear Reduction Box
designs.summary: A two-stage spur gear reduction assembly with housing, designed for a 5:1 speed reduction ratio. Includes all internal components: shafts, bearings, keys, and seals.

sections.heading: Design Overview
sections.text: This gear reduction box was designed to transmit 2.5 kW at 1440 RPM input speed, reducing it to 288 RPM output. The housing is a split-type design for ease of assembly and maintenance. All gear calculations follow AGMA standards.

sections.heading: Key Design Features
sections.text: The assembly includes helical-cut spur gears with involute profiles, deep-groove ball bearings at each shaft support, lip seals to prevent lubricant leakage, and an inspection cover. The housing is designed with adequate wall thickness for casting.

designs.title: Hydraulic Bottle Jack
designs.summary: Complete 3D model of a 20-ton hydraulic bottle jack with exploded view and engineering drawings. Modeled with accurate thread profiles and seal grooves.

sections.heading: Project Description
sections.text: A fully detailed 3D model of a 20-ton capacity hydraulic bottle jack. Every component — from the pump piston to the release valve — is modeled to manufacturer specifications with proper tolerances and surface finish callouts.

designs.title: Centrifugal Pump Impeller
designs.summary: Backward-curved centrifugal pump impeller with 6 blades, designed using Euler's turbomachinery equations. Includes draft analysis for casting feasibility.

sections.heading: Design Methodology
sections.text: The impeller was designed following Euler's pump equations to achieve the target head and flow rate. Blade angles were optimized to minimize flow separation and cavitation risk. Surface modeling techniques in SOLIDWORKS were used to create the complex blade geometry.

designs.title: Pipe Flange Assembly (ASME B16.5)
designs.summary: Weld neck flange assembly for a 4-inch Class 150 piping system, modeled per ASME B16.5 dimensional standards with bolt pattern and gasket.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This flange assembly follows ASME B16.5 dimensions for a 4-inch nominal pipe size, Class 150 rating. It includes weld neck flanges, a spiral wound gasket, and A193 B7 stud bolts with heavy hex nuts. Engineering drawings with full GD&T callouts are included.

simulations.title: Pressure Vessel Stress Analysis
simulations.summary: Static structural FEA of a cylindrical pressure vessel under 10 bar internal pressure. Evaluates von Mises stress distribution, deformation, and factor of safety against ASME criteria.

sections.heading: Problem Statement
sections.text: A cylindrical pressure vessel with hemispherical end caps is subjected to 10 bar internal gauge pressure. The objective is to verify that the von Mises stress remains below the allowable stress for SA-516 Grade 70 carbon steel, per ASME Section VIII Division 2.

sections.heading: Mesh & Boundary Conditions
sections.text: A hex-dominant mesh with 3 elements through the wall thickness was used. Mesh convergence study confirmed less than 2% change in peak stress with further refinement. Fixed support at the saddle locations, internal pressure applied on all inner surfaces.

sections.heading: Results & Discussion
sections.text: Peak von Mises stress of 142 MPa occurred at the head-to-shell junction, well below the 186 MPa allowable. Maximum total deformation was 0.23 mm at the vessel crown. The minimum factor of safety is 1.31. Results agree within 5% of ASME hand calculations.

simulations.title: External Aerodynamics of a Sedan Body
simulations.summary: Steady-state CFD simulation of airflow around a simplified sedan geometry at 100 km/h. Evaluates drag coefficient, pressure distribution, and wake structure.

sections.heading: Simulation Setup
sections.text: A simplified sedan body (Ahmed body variant) was placed in a virtual wind tunnel with dimensions 5L × 3W × 3H. Inlet velocity of 27.78 m/s (100 km/h), k-omega SST turbulence model, and standard air properties at 25°C. Steady-state RANS simulation using ANSYS Fluent.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Drag coefficient (Cd) was computed as 0.327, consistent with published data for similar geometries. Pressure recovery over the rear window shows the critical separation region. Streamline visualization reveals the recirculation zone behind the vehicle and vortex structures from the C-pillars.

simulations.title: Cantilever Beam Modal Analysis
simulations.summary: Modal analysis of a steel cantilever beam to extract the first 6 natural frequencies and mode shapes. Results validated against analytical solutions.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Determine the natural frequencies and mode shapes of a fixed-free steel beam (500 × 50 × 10 mm) to verify against Euler-Bernoulli beam theory and ensure operating frequencies are safely away from resonance.

simulations.title: Pipe Flow Heat Transfer
simulations.summary: Conjugate heat transfer CFD simulation of turbulent water flow through a heated copper pipe. Compares Nusselt number with Dittus-Boelter correlation.

sections.heading: Setup
sections.text: Turbulent water flow (Re = 15,000) through a 1-meter copper pipe with constant wall heat flux of 10,000 W/m². k-epsilon RNG turbulence model. Enhanced wall treatment with y+ < 1 near walls.

experience.title: Engineering Project Developer
experience.description: Designed and fabricated a low-cost pneumatic training system integrating Arduino-based control, pneumatic actuators, solenoid valves, and sequential operation logic. The project focused on demonstrating industrial automation principles through a practical, hands-on training platform.

education.title: BSc. in Industrial and Production Engineering
education.organization: Jashore University of Science and Technology
education.description: Pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Industrial and Production Engineering at Jashore University of Science and Technology (JUST), with a strong interest in computational engineering, advanced manufacturing, and data-driven problem-solving. My academic focus combines engineering fundamentals with Computer-Aided Design (CAD), Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), Finite Element Analysis (FEA), and Machine Learning.
